waterfront.name: Waterfront: Great Wheel, Pier 57, Aquarium & Overlook Walk
waterfront.blurb: The rebuilt Elliott Bay waterfront: the 175-ft Seattle Great Wheel over the water at Pier 57, Miners Landing, the Aquarium and the 2024 Overlook Walk bridge up to Pike Place.

spawn.note: New Alaskan Way promenade at the foot of Union St looking SW to the Wheel.
spawn.ground_elev_note: 40 m grid blends water (≈0 m) with the shore here; promenade/pier deck is ≈3–5 m — use OSM pier/coastline geometry.

extent.description: Alaskan Way promenade from University St (Pier 56) to Pier 60, Pier 57 deck and Miners Landing, Waterfront Park (Pier 57–58, rebuilt 2025), Aquarium plaza (Pier 59) and Ocean Pavilion, Overlook Walk ramp/stairs up to MarketFront.
extent.edges: Elliott Bay railings west; Alaskan Way traffic + bike lanes east; Overlook Walk connects to the pike-place scene (shared edge).
extent.vertical: Promenade ~3–5 m above sea level; Overlook Walk climbs ~20 m to MarketFront.

structures.name: Seattle Great Wheel (2012)
structures.form: White tubular-steel spoked wheel on a two-legged A-frame at the end of Pier 57, overhanging Elliott Bay; enclosed climate-controlled gondolas (one VIP gondola with glass floor); LED lighting along rim and spokes for night shows.

plaques.title: Over the water
plaques.text: At 175 ft the Great Wheel was the tallest Ferris wheel on the US West Coast when it opened on June 29, 2012, and extends 40 ft over Elliott Bay.

plaques.title: Pier 57
plaques.text: Built in 1902 for the John B. Agen Company, Pier 57 later served the Milwaukee Road railroad; the city traded it in 1989 for Piers 62/63.

plaques.title: Ocean Pavilion
plaques.text: The Aquarium's Ocean Pavilion, devoted to the Coral Triangle, opened in August 2024.

plaques.title: Overlook Walk
plaques.text: Completed in 2024, the Overlook Walk bridges Alaskan Way to link the waterfront with Pike Place Market.

interaction.primary: Ride the Great Wheel: 3 revolutions in a gondola, camera free-look, best photo at the top (53 m) facing the skyline.
secondary: Spot the seal (random idle on buoys)

iconic.frame: Great Wheel with gondolas lit against Elliott Bay at dusk

lines.text: Welcome aboard the Great Wheel! Three spins, about twelve minutes.
We hang about 40 feet out over Elliott Bay.
The wheel opened in 2012 — 175 feet tall, the biggest on the West Coast then.
Pier 57 was built in 1902. Ferries, steamships, fish processing — now carousel and chowder.
The new Overlook Walk takes you straight up to Pike Place.
They tore down the viaduct — this used to be all shadow and noise.
Ferry to Bainbridge is the cheapest cruise in town.
The bay's pretty even when it's grey.
Fish and chips on the pier, that's the plan.
Get the wheel AND the water!
Look, a seal!
Let's ride the Ferris wheel at night.
You can see the mountains across the water.
lines.orig: 海の向こうに山が見える。

lines.text: The aquarium has a new pavilion — let's go.
lines.orig: Das Aquarium hat einen neuen Pavillon — los geht's.

lines.text: One more with the ferry behind us.
lines.orig: पीछे फेरी के साथ एक और फोटो।

lines.text: The gulls want my fries!
We could take the ferry tomorrow.
lines.orig: On pourrait prendre le traversier demain.

lines.text: I want the gondola with the glass floor!
Watch your step on the pier boards!
Lunch walk. Got to get my steps in.
Music by the water, folks — enjoy!

dialogueGeneral.usage: Pedestrian set for the Seattle and Bellevue driving districts and as filler in every spot. ctx: greeting|bumped|photographed|idle|spot|rain|honked_at|near_miss; non-English lines carry orig+lang with English text.

tone.note: "Seattle Freeze": locals are described as "very polite but not particularly friendly" to strangers — keep local NPC lines courteous, brief, low-key; few unprompted chats.
Washington ranked 48th of 50 states for extraversion (2008 study cited by Wikipedia) — locals default to nods, "sorry", "you're good".

Honking is rare and seen as rude: ~3 in 4 Northwest drivers said they rarely or never honk (PEMCO 2017); attitudes softened by 2021 (65% say honking at least somewhat appropriate). NPC reaction to player honking near spots: surprised/disapproving, not aggressive.
Coffee culture: Seattle drinks more coffee than any other US city; espresso small talk is a safe icebreaker.
Rain talk is universal small talk; locals rarely use umbrellas (hoods/rain shells) — common local self-image, unsourced folklore: keep light.

Visitors: Canada was 73% of Seattle's 2.4 M international visitors in 2024; then China, India, UK, South Korea, Germany, Japan, Australia, France, Taiwan — languages used: English, French (Québec), Mandarin, Hindi, Korean, German, Japanese, Spanish (domestic + Latin America).
Indigenous art (totems, Salish Welcome): staff/guides speak respectfully; no jokes about sacred objects.
Guardrails: no stereotypes, accents written phonetically, slurs, politics or alcohol jokes about any group; tourists are curious and happy, locals helpful-but-reserved.
